title: Koriyama — 郡山
goal: Recognise school/student/teacher words and distinguish identity from action.

cards.title: A Transport Hub, a Learning Scene

blocks.text: Koriyama is a transport hub in Fukushima. We will use an invented classroom/learning scene. This is not a claim that a particular school accepts visitors or offers a course.
**郡山で文を読みました。** こおりやまで ぶんを よみました。 — I read sentences in Koriyama.

Reading and writing were introduced in Kakunodate. Today we name the people and place associated with study. A travel curriculum can add useful everyday situations while keeping exactly the fixed number of location lessons.

items: **Character:** 郡 · **Meaning/reading:** district; グン; こおり here · **Radical/components:** 邑 in right-side 阝/おおざと form, plus 君, a historical sound element · **Role:** Encounter. Right 阝 differs from left 阜/こざとへん despite similar shape.
**Character:** 山 · **Meaning/reading:** mountain; やま, サン · **Radical/components:** 山, やま; complete mountain-derived form · **Role:** Formal review.

blocks.text: **郡山 / こおりやま**. Keep the long **おお** sequence in こおり; do not read it as **こりやま** or guess **ぐんさん**. The city name does not make this lesson an administrative-district lesson. We inspect the difficult character but test only the familiar whole word/component distinction.

**学生 / がくせい — student; 学校 / がっこう — school**, introduced together and explained across the next cards. 学's radical is **子**, こ, below a cover-like **冖** and three small upper strokes. Do not label that cover 宀: 宀 includes a top dot that 冖 does not.

学 relates to learning/study. Its modern form helps recognition; **子** inside it does not make every student a small child. Adult students also exist. We prioritise useful compound words rather than require an isolated 学 reading as a conversational noun.
**私は学生です。** わたしは がくせいです。 — I am a student. The name of the role is a noun, not the verb “study.”

**学校 / がっこう — school.** 校 has radical **木**, きへん, with **交**, a historical sound element, on the right. The tree component gives an indexing/recognition connection, not a requirement that a school building must be wooden.
The compound has a small **っ**: **がっこう**, not **がくこう**. Its final **こう** has a long vowel.
**学校に行きます。** がっこうに いきます。 — I go to school.
**学校で本を読みます。** がっこうで ほんを よみます。 — I read a book at school.
Destination に and action-place で remain different. A new compound does not change the relationships already learned in shop and station scenes.

**学生 / がくせい — student; 先生 / せんせい — teacher**, high-priority whole words. 生 is its own radical, うまれる/いきる. Its whole shape is historically growth/life-related; do not try to derive every modern role word from a literal plant picture.

生 is **せい** in both compounds. In other common words its reading changes, but we reserve 生まれる / うまれる for a later daily-life/family expansion. “Knowing 生” does not mean memorising all its possible readings immediately.
**友だちは学生です。** ともだちは がくせいです。 — My friend is a student. The same role can apply to different people without changing the word's reading.

**先生 / せんせい — teacher; 先 / さき — ahead/before, an orientation word.** 先 is indexed under **儿**, ひとあし. Notice its upper earth/step-like strokes and the two lower leg-shaped strokes. Those are not the same side radical as **亻** in 住.
**この人は先生です。** この ひとは せんせいです。 — This person is a teacher.

先生 can be used as a respectful title in appropriate contexts. Here the intended role is teacher. It is not the ordinary plural of 学生 or a special counter. **先週 / せんしゅう**, last week, is a later time-word expansion when 週 is studied.

cards.title: Identity Is Different from an Activity

blocks.text: **私は学生です。** わたしは がくせいです。 — I am a student.
**私は本を読みます。** わたしは ほんを よみます。 — I read a book.
**友だちは先生です。** ともだちは せんせいです。 — My friend is a teacher.

One identifies a role; another describes an action. Reading a book once does not prove someone is a student, and writing a sentence does not prove they are a teacher. Test questions use explicit role statements rather than ask the learner to infer social roles from an unrelated activity.
**何を読みますか / なにをよみますか — What do you read?** contrasts with **何ですか / なんですか**. The whole phrase determines 何's useful reading.

items: **Meaning:** is a student · **Japanese:** 学生です · **Reading:** がくせいです
**Meaning:** is not a student · **Japanese:** 学生ではありません · **Reading:** がくせいではありません
**Meaning:** was a student · **Japanese:** 学生でした · **Reading:** がくせいでした
**Meaning:** was not a student · **Japanese:** 学生ではありませんでした · **Reading:** がくせいではありませんでした

blocks.text: These noun forms were completed in Yamagata's weather lesson. They apply to a role noun as well as a weather noun. **学生がいません** instead means there is no student present; it does not say that a particular person is not a student. Keep negative identity and negative existence separate.
**教室 / きょうしつ — classroom.** 教/室 remain assisted characters; they will receive fuller formal attention later. A useful whole word can be explained before every constituent kanji is assigned mastery.
**教室に先生がいます。** きょうしつに せんせいが います。 — There is a teacher in the classroom.
**教室で文を書きます。** きょうしつで ぶんを かきます。 — I write a sentence in the classroom.
**先生に聞きます。** せんせいに ききます。 — I ask the teacher.
We now connect the asking-person pattern from Tsuruoka to a new role. The teacher's identity and the place of writing are supplied clearly.
**郡山で先生に会いました。先生の名前はゆきです。** こおりやまで せんせいに あいました。せんせいの なまえは ゆきです。 — I met a teacher in Koriyama. The teacher's name is Yuki.
**学校で本を読みました。そして、ノートに文を書きました。** がっこうで ほんを よみました。そして、ノートに ぶんを かきました。 — I read a book at school. Then I wrote a sentence in a notebook.

The named teacher is fictional. Meeting someone uses に; the action place uses で; writing surface uses に. We reuse the same relationships with a new topic instead of expecting learners to translate particles mechanically.

items: Read 郡山, 学生, 学校 and 先生. **Answer:** こおりやま; がくせい; がっこう; せんせい.
Which radical links 学 with 字? **Answer:** 子.
What visible radical links 校 with 松? **Answer:** 木.
Make 学生です past negative. **Answer:** 学生ではありませんでした.
Complete “ask a teacher”: 先生＿聞きます。 **Answer:** に.
Does 本を読みます alone establish that the person is a student? **Answer:** No; an explicit role statement is needed.

blocks.text: 郡山 is こおりやま. Right-side 阝 is the 邑/おおざと family in 郡. 学生/学校/先生 are がくせい/がっこう/せんせい. 学 and 字 share 子; 校 has 木. A role noun uses です/ではありません/でした/ではありませんでした. Negative role identification is different from absence of a person.
**Recall task:** “I am a student. I read a book at school.” **Model:** 私は学生です。学校で本を読みます。 Continue to Iwaki and talk about languages.
